item.title: Seniors embrace Tesla automated driving technology despite questions about safety
item.description: Older drivers are using Tesla's automated driving technology to stay on the road longer. But safety experts warn the company may be over-selling what its cars can do.

item.title: Let's talk turkey: Here's how Thanksgiving meal costs have changed this year
item.description: Grocery costs have been on the rise, but food-price analysts say it's unclear if you'll spend more on the Thanksgiving meal this year. Some people are deciding not to host or are hosting fewer guests.

item.title: As holidays approach, food banks face increased demand
item.description: Under pressure from higher grocery prices, more people turn to food banks. NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with Linda Nageotte of Feeding America, a nonprofit running a network of food banks.

item.title: Army reschedules detonation of toxic explosives in Iowa for Wednesday
item.description: The U.S. Army has rescheduled the detonation of about five tons of bomb-making material in Iowa to Wednesday to accommodate weather and "mitigation measures."

item.title: Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly
item.description: It's not easy to retrieve foreign objects from animals once ingested. Some things can be grabbed using an endoscope. But if an item gets far into the intestinal tract, surgery isn't always possible.

item.title: Chicago now has the worst traffic in the U.S. — here's why
item.description: Traffic is bad in many U.S. cities, but Chicago is the worst. Years of construction are causing record delays on the freeway between downtown and O'Hare Airport.

item.title: Medicare looks a bit different in 2027, so don't miss open enrollment
item.description: Open enrollment for Medicare runs through Dec. 7, and there are a few different pitfalls people should watch out for this year. Your drug plan or Medicare Advantage plan could be changing a lot.
